title: Russian Drone and Glide Bomb Barrage Hits Kyiv, Sumy, Kherson, Kharkiv Regions, Kills 5
detail: Russian forces struck Kyiv, Sumy, Kherson, and Kharkiv regions through the day on August 28, killing 5 people and injuring at least 33. In Kyiv region, 1 person was killed and 2 injured in early morning attacks that damaged 14 warehouses, 16 private houses, 3 apartment buildings, and 16 vehicles, and destroyed a Nova Poshta postal sorting center with 4 glide bombs. In Sumy region, a drone strike using a 'double tap' tactic — a second drone hitting the same site after emergency crews arrived — killed a 61-year-old man and wounded 7 (4 hospitalized). In Kherson region, strikes killed 1 person and injured 11 (including 1 child); Russia has dropped roughly 170 guided glide bombs on the region since July 1 as part of what officials described as a campaign to 'weaponize winter' by targeting the power grid — regional head Oleksandr Prokudin warned Kherson could be without electricity 'not for hours or days, but for a long time.' In Kharkiv region, 2 people (ages 26 and 38) were killed and 13 injured, including 2 children. Ukrainian government official Andrii Kovalenko said the goal of the dispersed strikes was 'to exhaust air defenses and the population.'

title: Russian Drone Strikes Ammunition Depot Near Kyiv, Killing 37 — Deadliest Attack of 2026
detail: A Russian Geran-4 attack drone struck a Ukrainian military ammunition depot in the village of Myla, roughly 5 km west of Kyiv along the Kyiv-Chop highway (Bucha district, Kyiv Oblast), at approximately 20:10 local time on August 28, triggering successive detonations of shells, mines, and other munitions. The blast and resulting fires killed at least 37 people — 34 of them residents of a nearby care home for the elderly and disabled — injured 42 (including 4 children), and left 4 people missing as of Aug 29, 17:00 local time. More than 300 emergency responders evacuated 381 people, including 59 children, and at least 130 residential buildings were damaged. It was the war's deadliest single attack of 2026, surpassing a July 2 strike that killed 31. President Zelensky called it 'terrible negligence' for storing explosives next to residential areas, and Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office opened a criminal negligence investigation into the depot's storage legality and permits. Russia's Defense Ministry said it had targeted a warehouse storing components and launch boosters for Ukrainian long-range drones. Local resident Oleksandr Vodolaz said 'no one knew that weapons were stored there.'

media.caption: Emergency responders at the site of a Russian drone strike on an ammunition depot in Myla, Bucha district, August 28-29, 2026

title: Zelensky Sets Target of 1,000 Long-Range Drones Per Day Against Russia
detail: In his evening address on August 28, President Zelensky called for Ukraine to more than triple its long-range drone strike campaign against Russia, to 1,000 drones a day. 'The task is a thousand drones for long-range strikes against Russia every day. Right now, the average is over 300 of our long-range strikes, there must be more,' he said. He tied the escalation to strengthening defenses against jet-powered Shahed drones and stepping up deep strikes on Russian territory as Moscow intensifies its own aerial campaign against Ukrainian cities. The announcement came the same day Ukrainian forces struck the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl and a Tu-95MS strategic bomber at Engels-2 airbase.

title: Ukraine Strikes Tu-95MS Bomber at Engels Airbase and Yaroslavl Oil Refinery
detail: In an overnight operation into August 28, Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) Alpha special forces unit struck a Russian Tu-95MS strategic bomber-missile carrier at the Engels-2 airbase in Saratov Oblast — a major hub for Russia's Tu-95MS/Tu-160 fleet used to launch Kh-101 cruise missiles at Ukraine. In a coordinated strike the same night, Ukrainian long-range drones hit the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl (about 250 km northeast of Moscow, roughly 700 km from the Ukrainian border) — one of Russia's five largest refineries, processing around 15 million tons of oil annually — sparking multiple fires; it was the eighth Ukrainian strike on the facility in 2026. President Zelensky confirmed both strikes, as well as additional hits on Black Sea targets and the Kstovo refinery.
